subject: Execution cadence, canary migration & training plan — VelocityX onboarding
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@velocityx.com>, Alyssa Ford <alyssa.ford@velocityx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Execution cadence, canary migration & training plan — VelocityX onboarding

Hi Daniel / Alyssa,

Thanks again for signing — excited to get VelocityX into production. Attached is an initial execution cadence I sketched after our post-signature call. The file (VX_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) contains a week-by-week breakdown, owner assignments, minimal acceptance criteria and a short canary checklist.

High-level proposed milestones:
- Week 1: Kickoff, environment provisioning, runbook handoff
- Week 2–3: Integration testing + first canary (10% traffic, automated fallback)
- Week 4: Canary evaluation and training for power users
- Week 5: Staged ramp to 50% with continued monitoring
- Week 7: Full cutover and runbook transition to VelocityX ops

Ask for this week: can you confirm the two attendees for the training pilot (names + technical contacts)? Also confirm your preferred weekday window for the weekly 30-minute sync (we've proposed Tuesdays 11–11:30 PT).

I attached a concise canary-checklist.pdf and slides for the training cadence. I’ll loop in Jonas to coordinate the infra prerequisites.

Thanks,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Execution cadence, canary migration & training plan — VelocityX onboarding

Soojin — thanks for the doc and the clear milestones. Quick answers:
- Training pilot attendees: Alyssa Ford (product lead) and Marco Santos (platform engineer, marco.santos@velocityx.com).
- Weekly sync: Tuesdays 11:00 PT works for us.

On the canary specifics, we’d like an initial duration of 72 hours for the 10% window to get enough signal from our event stream. Also can you confirm what rollback triggers you recommend (error rate, latency, degradation in top-k accuracy)?

– Daniel
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@velocityx.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Execution cadence, canary migration & training plan — VelocityX onboarding

Daniel — good notes. For rollback triggers we typically recommend the following (we can tune per workload):
- Error rate > 2x baseline OR absolute increase > 0.5% (whichever yields faster detection)
- Token-generation latency P95 increase > 150ms over baseline
- Model quality regression: top-k metric drop > 3% on the live eval set or a sustained drop on the customer-provided golden prompts

We propose the 72-hour canary you requested. During that window we will run a short evaluation suite every 12 hours (automated) and a human review at 48h if any anomaly flags. If all gates pass, we’ll move to the ramp to 50% across next two weeks. See canary-checklist.pdf (attachment) for the gating procedure.

Marissa

2) For the human review cadence, could we have a short runbook that lists who performs the review and the exact decision matrix (approve / hold / rollback)?

If you can add those into the MAP doc we can sign off on the 72-hour canary.

– Daniel

Daniel / team — I’ve updated the MAP workbook in Drive with the KV-cache validation steps and a short human-review runbook (see link below). Summary of added items:
- KV-cache validation: synthetic run targeting median prompt lengths, 1k sample, validate correctness and cache hit-rate > 75% for warm paths
- Human review runbook: who (Redwood SRE on-call + VelocityX product lead), checklist (latency, error windows, top-k comparison), decision matrix (Approve: no gate failures; Hold: transient anomalies but stable; Rollback: gate failure thresholds exceeded)
- I also appended the training-cadence-slides.pptx with a 60-min lab agenda for the pilot session.

Next steps:
- Soojin to confirm Tuesday 11:00 PT recurring invite and attach the final MAP export.
- Daniel to confirm sign-off on the 72-hour canary by EOD Monday.

Vivek
